kind.description: Talisman, Ash, Tear, Consumable or Spell.

slot.description: Which slot it occupies, and so whether it multiplies with the others.

multiplier.description: Its figure for this hit kind.

applies_on.description: The hit kinds it is worth more than 1.0 on. Quote it when saying why a buff did not count.

state_conditional.description: True when it is above 1.0 on every hit kind, which means its condition is a state — a bleed proc, full HP — and not the kind of hit.

note.description: The table's own wording for when it applies.

cost.description: What the bonus is paid for, when the description says. The Scorpion Charms buy their 1.12 with ten points of physical negation, and quoting the bonus without the cost is half an answer.

multiplier.description: The product of what applied. 1.0 when nothing did, which is the honest answer for a hit none of these buffs touches.

not_counted.description: Buffs held that did not go into the product, each with why — wrong kind of hit, a state not asserted, or overwritten by another buff in the same slot. This is the actionable half of the answer.

slot_rules.description: Multiply, Overwrite or Identity, per slot. The reason two Golden Vows are not 1.15 x 1.15.

damage_multiplier.description: The same figure shaped for optimal-affinity's damage_multiplier, so nothing reshapes it downstream.

hit_kinds.description: Every hit kind the table distinguishes.

unknown.description: Names given that BuffMult.csv and the damage-source table have never heard of. Non-empty means no stack was computed: `multiplier` is 1.0 and `applied` is empty, because a product that quietly leaves a buff out is worse than no product at all.

known_buffs.description: Every buff name the tables do know, returned only when `unknown` is non-empty so the caller can correct the name without a second call.
